title: The Beguiling Boy 5
content:
(a/n- Da-ge= eldest brother, er-ge= second brother)

He kicked his own saber away, sending it skittering across the dirt, and bolted from the training grounds.

Behind him, Jin Guangyao shouted, "Huaisang! Huaisang!" He moved to give chase, but Nie Mingjue’s icy voice cut through the air: "Stand down."

Jin Guangyao froze mid-stride, turning back. Nie Mingjue shot him a glare, barely keeping his temper on a leash. "You still have the nerve to show your face here?"

Jin Guangyao kept his voice low and humble. "I came to apologize."

Man, Wei Wuxian thought, this guy’s skin is thicker than mine.

"You? Acknowledge a mistake?" Nie Mingjue sneered.

Before Jin Guangyao could reply, the disciples sent to fetch the medicine rushed back. "Sect Leader, Lianfang-zun... the Second Young Master bolted his door from the inside. He won't let anyone in."

"Let's see how long he can keep it locked," Nie Mingjue growled. "Rebellious little brat!"

Jin Guangyao turned to the disciples with an easy, reassuring smile. "Thank you for the trouble. Leave the ointment with me; I'll take it to him in a bit."

He took the porcelain jar, waiting until the disciples bowed and scattered before facing the older man.

Nie Mingjue crossed his arms. "What are you really doing here?"

"Did Da-ge forget?" Jin Guangyao asked softly. "Today is our scheduled day for the zither."

Nie Mingjue cut straight to the bone. "When it comes to Xue Yang, there is no negotiation. Don't waste your breath trying to butter me up. It won't work."

Jin Guangyao countered smoothly, "First of all, I'm not buttering you up. Second, if it truly doesn't work, why should Da-ge be so wary of my flattery?"

Nie Mingjue clamped his jaw shut, remaining silent.

"Da-ge, you've been pushing Huaisang harder and harder lately... Is it because of your saber spirit?" He paused, watching the older man's face carefully. "Does Huaisang still not know about the family curse?"

"Why should he know this early?" Nie Mingjue snapped.

Jin Guangyao let out a quiet sigh. "Huaisang was spoiled rotten, but he can't spend his entire life playing the idle second young master of Qinghe. One day, he'll realize you were only acting in his best interest. Just like... eventually, I realized Da-ge was only doing what was best for me."

Wei Wuxian was genuinely floored. I have to hand it to him—I wouldn't be able to utter something that sickeningly sweet in two lifetimes, yet Jin Guangyao delivers it without missing a beat. It actually sounds touching.

Nie Mingjue wasn't so easily swayed. "If you truly understand, then bring me Xue Yang's severed head."

Without a second's hesitation, Jin Guangyao replied, "Fine."

Nie Mingjue stared down at him. Meeting his gaze unflinchingly, Jin Guangyao repeated, "Fine. Just grant me one final chance. Within two months, I will personally bring you Xue Yang's head."

"And if you fail?"

Jin Guangyao's voice was unwavering. "If I fail, my life is yours to dispose of."

Wei Wuxian couldn't help but feel a strange sense of respect.

Every single time, Jin Guangyao was terrified out of his wits by Nie Mingjue, yet through sheer silver-tongued rhetoric and intricate maneuvering, he always managed to wrangle another chance out of the man. That very night, Jin Guangyao sat serenely inside the Unclean Realm, calmly plucking out the Song of Clarity as if nothing had ever happened.

He had sworn that oath with absolute conviction, but Nie Mingjue never even lived to see those two months through.

Sometime later, during a martial exhibition hosted by the Qinghe Nie Sect, Nie Mingjue was walking past a guest pavilion when he caught the muffled sound of voices. It sounded like Jin Guangyao. A beat later, another familiar voice joined in.

Lan Xichen murmured, "Since Da-ge swore that oath of brotherhood with you in the first place, it means he acknowledges you."

Jin Guangyao's voice was heavy with bitter exhaustion. "Er-ge, did you not hear the words he used during our oath? Every single phrase was pointed. 'Condemned by thousands, torn apart by five horses'—he was clearly warning me. I... I have never heard such an ominous oath of brotherhood before..."

Lan Xichen comforted him gently, "He said 'should one harbor treacherous intent'. Do you? If you don't, why let it weigh on your mind?"

"I don't! But Da-ge has already made up his mind that I do, so what choice do I have?"

"He has always valued your talents," Lan Xichen replied. "He only wants you to walk the right path."

"It's not that I don't know right from wrong; it's that sometimes, my hands are tied. Right now, I'm walking on thin ice everywhere I turn, walking on eggshells around everyone. I can take it from strangers, but have I ever wronged Da-ge? Er-ge, you heard him yourself—did you hear the venom he spat at me last time?"

Lan Xichen sighed. "He was caught up in the heat of the moment, speaking without thinking. Da-ge's temper isn't what it used to be, so you must take care not to provoke him. The saber spirit's backlash has been tormenting him severely, and his fight with Huaisang still hasn't blown over."

Jin Guangyao choked back a sob. "If he can say such things in a momentary fit of anger, what does he truly think of me behind closed doors? Just because I couldn't choose my birth, just because my mother couldn't choose her fate, does that mean I deserve to be trampled like dirt for the rest of my life? If that's the case, how is Da-ge any different from the ones who look down on me? No matter what I achieve, in the end, a single phrase from him strips it all away: 'the son of a whore.'"

Here he was, crying on Lan Xichen's shoulder, yet only the night before he had been the picture of gentle devotion, playing the zither and sharing quiet conversation with Nie Mingjue. Hearing him stir up gossip and slander behind his back, Nie Mingjue’s fury erupted. He kicked the door off its hinges, incandescent rage burning through his veins as a thunderous roar tore from his chest:

"How dare you, you insolent bastard!"

The sight of him drained the color from Jin Guangyao's face; his soul practically left his body as he scrambled behind Lan Xichen. Caught between the two, Lan Xichen barely had time to open his mouth before Nie Mingjue’s saber came whistling down. Lan Xichen drew his blade to parry the strike, shouting, "Run!"

Jin Guangyao bolted through the shattered doorway. Nie Mingjue shoved Lan Xichen aside, growling, "Out of my way!" and charged after him.

Rounding a covered corridor, he suddenly saw Jin Guangyao leisurely strolling toward him. He brought his saber down in a savage arc, spraying gore across the floorboards. But wait—Jin Guangyao had been running for dear life, so how could he possibly be ambling back with such casual ease?!

Staggering past the fresh kill, Nie Mingjue stumbled onto the central training grounds, panting heavily. In Wei Wuxian's ears, the frantic, deafening thud of his racing heart hammered like a war drum.

Jin Guangyao!

Across the entire square, emerging from every corridor, every single face in the crowd was Jin Guangyao!

Nie Mingjue had suffered a complete qi deviation!

His sanity shattered, his mind was locked onto a single, bloodthirsty instinct: kill, kill, kill Jin Guangyao. He swung his blade at anything that moved, screams of terror erupting in every direction.

Suddenly, a desperate, agonized shriek pierced through the haze: "Da-ge!"

The sound struck Nie Mingjue like a bucket of ice water, pulling a shred of clarity back into his clouded mind. He whipped around, squinting through the sea of mocking Jin Guangyaos until he finally recognized a different face.

Nie Huaisang was clutching a bleeding slash across his arm, dragging an injured leg as he limped toward him. Seeing his brother freeze, tears spilled over his cheeks in trembling relief. "Da-ge! Da-ge, it's me! Put the saber down, it's me!"

Before Nie Huaisang could reach him, Nie Mingjue collapsed.

As his vision faded, the madness cleared from his eyes, and he finally caught sight of the real Jin Guangyao.

Standing at the far end of the colonnade, not a single speck of blood marred his pristine robes. He was staring back at the carnage, twin tracks of tears streaming silently down his cheeks.

Yet the blooming Sparks Amidst Snow crest on his chest seemed to smile in his place.

Suddenly, Wei Wuxian heard a distant voice calling his name.

The tone was cool and deep, faint and hollow at first, like a phantom whisper bridging a dream. The second call was sharper, closer, laced with an imperceptible thread of raw panic.

By the third call, it rang crystal clear:

"Wei Ying!"

The sound snapped his tether, and Wei Wuxian forcefully tore himself from the memory!

He was back in his paper-doll vessel, plastered flat against the iron helmet sealing Nie Mingjue’s severed head. The iron visor covering the face had been loosened by his earlier prying, revealing a single bloodshot, wide-open eye glaring out in frozen fury.

Time was running out; he had to return to his physical body immediately!

Paper-Xian shook out his sleeves, taking flight like a fluttering moth. But the instant he slipped past the talismanic curtain, he froze—a silhouette was waiting in the shadows of the secret vault.

Jin Guangyao smiled faintly. Without a word, he drew a slender, flexible blade from his belt—his infamous sword, Hensheng.

Back when he operated deep undercover at Wen Ruohan's side, Jin Guangyao had kept this pliable blade coiled around his waist or strapped to his forearm, unleashing it during critical ambushes. Though Hensheng’s edge appeared supple and gentle as flowing water, its strikes were lethally venomous, clinging to its target like a relentless wraith. Once its flexible steel coiled around an enemy's weapon, a burst of perverse spiritual energy from Jin Guangyao could snap a masterwork blade into jagged pieces; countless sacred swords had been reduced to scrap metal that way.

Now, the blade whipped through the air like a shimmering silver viper, snapping at the paper doll's heels. A single graze from its fangs would shred the paper—and Wei Wuxian's soul—to ribbons.

Paper-Xian fluttered desperately, darting left and right with frantic agility, but operating in a fragile paper shell severely limited his reflexes. After dodging several near-misses, the tip of the blade grazed his sleeve. If this kept up, he was going to be skewered!

Out of the corner of his eye, he spotted a longsword resting quietly on an open wooden display shelf against the wall. Untouched for years, a thick layer of dust coated the scabbard and the surrounding masonry.

It was his old sword—Suibian!

Paper-Xian dived toward the shelf, stomping down with all his might against the hilt. With a crisp, ringing clang, the spiritual blade answered its master's call, springing clear of its scabbard!

Suibian shot into the air, instantly locking into a ferocious clash with Hensheng’s sinister silver light. A flash of pure shock flickered across Jin Guangyao's face, though he masked it in a heartbeat. Snapping his wrist, he guided Hensheng to coil around Suibian’s straight blade like a twisting vine, then let go, leaving the two spiritual weapons to duel on their own while his left hand whipped a talisman straight toward Wei Wuxian!

The talisman burst into roaring flames midair. Searing heat washed over him, but taking advantage of the blinding clash between the two swords, Wei Wuxian flapped his paper sleeves and shot out of the secret vault like an arrow!

His spiritual timer had run down to the absolute dregs; abandoning all pretense of stealth, he barreled through the corridors back to the guest quarters. Just as Lan Wangji cracked the door open, the paper scrap dived forward with everything it had—smacking squarely onto Lan Wangji’s face.

Paper-Xian clung desperately to his cheek, fluttering and trembling like a leaf in a gale. With his wide paper sleeves blocking both of Lan Wangji's eyes, the Second Young Master Lan simply stood there, letting the paper doll quiver against his skin for a few seconds before gently peeling it off with two fingers.

A breath later, the soul snapped back into its vessel. Wei Wuxian drew in a sharp, ragged gasp, throwing his head back as his eyes flew open. He scrambled to his feet, but his physical senses hadn't aligned yet; dizziness washed over him, and he tipped forward, right into Lan Wangji’s waiting arms.

Before he could steady himself, Wei Wuxian jerked his head up, cracking the crown of his skull straight into Lan Wangji's jaw.

Crack! Both men let out a muffled groan.

Rubbing his sore head with one hand while reaching up to touch Lan Wangji’s chin with the other, Wei Wuxian stammered, "Ow! Sorry, sorry! Lan Zhan, you alright?"

Lan Wangji gently caught his wrist, steering his hand away with a subtle shake of his head.

Wei Wuxian tugged at his sleeve. "Move!"

Lan Wangji fell into step without questioning him, only asking once they were through the threshold, "Where?"

"The Fragrance Hall! That bronze mirror inside is the entrance to a secret vault! His wife stumbled onto something she shouldn't have and he dragged her inside—she should still be in there! And Chifeng-zun's head is in there too!"

Jin Guangyao would undoubtedly reinforce the wards on Nie Mingjue’s skull and move it, but while you could smuggle a severed head, you couldn't smuggle away Qin Su! She was the lady of Koi Tower; having just attended the banquet, if a living person of her stature vanished into thin air, questions would be asked. They had to strike right now, cutting through the red tape before Jin Guangyao had time to spin a cover story or silence his witnesses!

The two of them tore through the compound like a landslide, kicking aside anyone in their path. Jin Guangyao had drilled his guards around the Fragrance Hall to stay alert, instructing them to raise the alarm if anyone breached the perimeter even if they couldn't stop them. But right now, their vigilance worked against him. The louder their warning sirens blared, the worse it was for the master of Koi Tower. With dozens of prominent clans gathered for the conference, the racket wouldn't just warn Jin Guangyao—it would drag the entire cultivation world straight to his doorstep!

Jin Ling was the first to arrive, his sword already drawn, looking thoroughly confused. "What are you two doing here?!"

Lan Wangji ignored him, taking the jade steps three at a time as Bichen slid from its sheath.

Jin Ling bristled, raising his guard. "This is my youngest uncle's private bedchamber! Did you lose your way? No, wait—you broke in! What do you think you're doing?!"

The courtyard was quickly swarming with sect leaders and guest cultivators, their murmurs rippling through the night air:

"What's happening?"
"Why is it so noisy over here?"
"This is the Fragrance Hall... isn't barging in here inappropriate...?"
"We heard the defense alarms go off..."

Unease hung thick in the air, but the bedchamber itself remained dead silent.

Wei Wuxian rapped a knuckle against the door. "Sect Leader Jin? Chief Cultivator?"

Jin Ling snarled, "What are you playing at?! You brought a whole mob with you! This is my uncle's personal quarters, his bedchamber, you hear me?! Didn't I warn you to stay—"

Lan Xichen stepped forward, his eyes locking with Lan Wangji's. A flicker of shock crossed the older brother's face, melting into an agonizingly complex expression of disbelief.

He understood.

Nie Mingjue’s head was inside this hall.

Right on cue, an easy, smiling voice drifted from behind the crowd: "What is all this commotion? Was our hospitality lacking today, that everyone feels compelled to throw a midnight banquet at my door?"

Jin Guangyao strolled leisurely through the parted crowd.

Wei Wuxian smirked. "Lianfang-zun arrives right on time. A moment later, and no one would get to see what's hidden inside your secret vault."

Jin Guangyao blinked, looking mildly surprised. "Secret vault?"

Murmurs of suspicion broke out among the onlookers.

Jin Guangyao looked around with an innocent shrug. "What about it? A secret vault is hardly unusual, is it? Any clan with a few ancestral treasures to its name keeps a vault or two."

Before Lan Wangji could speak, Lan Xichen cut in. His tone was quiet, but unyielding:

"A-Yao, open the doors. Let us inspect the vault."

Jin Guangyao’s brow furrowed in polite bewilderment, looking slightly put out. "Er-ge, if it's called a treasure vault, the things inside are meant to be kept private. Demanding I open it out of nowhere... this is..."

In such a short window, there was no way Jin Guangyao could have smuggled Qin Su out. Teleportation talismans only transported the caster, and in her shattered state, she lacked both the spiritual energy and the will to use one. She had to be inside.

Dead or alive, her presence alone would be fatal to him.

Yet even backed into a corner, Jin Guangyao remained remarkably poised, making excuses. But the more he deflected, the firmer Lan Xichen's voice became:

"Open it."

Jin Guangyao held his sworn brother's gaze for a long moment, then broke into a radiant smile. "Since Er-ge insists, I suppose I have no choice but to let everyone have a look."

Stepping up to the entrance, he waved a hand, and the heavy double doors swung open.

From the crowd, a cold voice sneered, "Rumor had it the Gusu Lan Clan prized propriety above all else, but it seems rumors are just rumors. Forcing your way into another sect leader's private bedchamber—truly the height of propriety."

Wei Wuxian remembered hearing Jin disciples addressing this man earlier as "Sect Leader Su"—Su She, the rising leader of the Moling Su Sect. Dressed in crisp white robes, Su She had narrow eyes, thin brows, and delicate lips—handsome, in an arrogant sort of way, but entirely unremarkable.

Jin Guangyao waved it off with an easy chuckle. "Never mind, never mind. It's not like I'm hiding anything shameful."

His tone was calibrated to perfection—sounding endlessly patient, yet carrying just the right hint of awkward embarrassment to make the intruders look like bullies. Trailing behind his uncle, Jin Ling glared daggers at Wei Wuxian, fuming over the breach of privacy.

"You wished to see the treasure vault, yes?" Jin Guangyao asked.

He pressed his hand against the bronze mirror, traced an invisible talisman across the metal, and stepped through the looking glass. Wei Wuxian followed immediately, stepping back into the secret vault.

There was the ward-covered curtain on the display shelf. There was the cold iron slaughtering table.

And there was Qin Su.

She stood by the iron slab with her back turned to them. Lan Xichen blinked in surprise. "Why is Madame Jin in here?"

Jin Guangyao explained smoothly, "Everything we own is shared. A-Su drops by to look through the collection all the time."

Wei Wuxian stared at her back, stunned. He didn't move her, and he didn't kill her? Isn't he afraid she'll talk?

Uneasy, he circled around to study her face. She was alive, breathing, and showing no signs of physical distress. Though her expression was utterly blank, Wei Wuxian could tell her spiritual veins were unblocked; she wasn't under a spell, nor was she poisoned. Her mind was completely lucid.

And that only made the scene a hundred times more terrifying.

He had witnessed firsthand how hysterical and repulsed she had been by Jin Guangyao only an incense stick ago. How on earth could Jin Guangyao have struck a deal to muzzle her so quickly?

Dread coiled in his gut; this wasn't going as planned. Striding up to the display shelf, Wei Wuxian grabbed the warding curtain and ripped it aside!

Behind the cloth sat no iron helmet, and certainly no severed head.

Only an ornate dagger.

The blade radiated a chilling, malevolent bloodlust. Lan Xichen, who had been staring at the curtain with quiet dread, let out an audible sigh of relief upon seeing the blade. "What is this?"

"Ah, that," Jin Guangyao said, strolling over to pluck the dagger from the shelf, turning it casually in his hands. "A rare curiosity. It once belonged to an assassin; it's razor-sharp and has claimed countless lives. If you look closely at the blade, you'll find the reflection staring back isn't yours. Sometimes it shows a man, sometimes a woman, sometimes an elder—each shadow is a vengeful spirit slain by its edge. The yin energy was far too heavy, so I hung a warding curtain to keep it sealed."

Lan Xichen frowned. "Could this be...?"

Jin Guangyao nodded easily. "Indeed. A relic of Wen Ruohan."

The man was terrifyingly sharp. He had anticipated that this vault might be exposed one day, so alongside Nie Mingjue’s remains, he had stocked the shelves with authentic treasures—swords, talismans, ancient rubbings, and spiritual tools. The room looked for all the world like a standard clan treasury. The dagger was genuinely dark and historic, and collecting cursed war trophies from the Sunshot Campaign was a common hobby among the great sects.

Everything appeared entirely above board.

Standing at Jin Guangyao's side, watching him casually turn the blade in his fingers, Qin Su’s hand suddenly shot out, snatching the dagger from his grip!

Her facial muscles spasmed, twisting into an agonizing grimace. To the onlookers, the expression was indecipherable, but Wei Wuxian—having eavesdropped on their private confrontation—understood it instantly.

Agony, fury, and unbearable shame!

Jin Guangyao's smile froze. "A-Su?"

Both Lan Wangji and Wei Wuxian lunged forward to disarm her, but Qin Su twisted her body away—and plunged the blade hilt-deep into her own stomach!

Jin Guangyao let out a bloodcurdling cry: "A-Su!"

He lunged forward, catching her collapsing frame as Lan Xichen scrambled to administer healing elixirs. But the dagger was too sharp, its demonic malice far too virulent; within seconds, Qin Su had breathed her last!

The entire vault froze in horrified shock. No one had seen the suicide coming. Jin Guangyao sobbed his wife's name over and over, cradling her face in his trembling hands, tears streaming down his cheeks to splash against her cold skin.

Lan Xichen murmured, deeply shaken, "A-Yao... my condolences..."

Jin Guangyao looked up, his eyes bloodshot and wide with grief. "Er-ge, what is happening? Why did A-Su take her own life? And why did you all gather outside my hall, demanding I open this vault? Is there something you haven't told me?"

Jiang Cheng, having just pushed through the crowd, demanded in an icy tone, "Ze-wu-jun, you had better explain this clearly. The rest of us are completely in the dark."

With the crowd clamoring for answers, Lan Xichen had no choice but to speak. "Some time ago, disciples of our sect encountered a severed left arm while night-hunting in Mo Village. It carried monstrous resentment, and Wangji has been tracking its guidance ever since. Once we gathered the rest of the dismembered limbs, we discovered the identity of the corpse... was Da-ge."

An uproar exploded across the hall!

Jin Guangyao gasped in sheer horror. "Da-ge?! But Da-ge was laid to rest! You and I attended his burial with our own eyes!"

Nie Huaisang looked as though his mind had shattered, babbling incoherently, "Da-ge? Xichen-ge, are you talking about my brother?! Your brother?!"

Lan Xichen offered a grim, heavy nod. Nie Huaisang’s eyes rolled back into his head, and he passed out cold, dropping flat onto the floor. The crowd descended into chaos: "Sect Leader Nie!" "Get a medic, quickly!"

Tears still clung to Jin Guangyao's lashes, but his knuckles were white, trembling with righteous fury. "Dismembered... torn apart! Who could commit such a monstrous, sickening atrocity?!"

Lan Xichen shook his head. "We do not know. When it came to finding the head, the trail went cold."

Jin Guangyao froze, understanding dawning on his face. "The trail went cold... so you came looking for it here?"

Lan Xichen looked away in guilty silence.

Jin Guangyao stared at him in utter heartbreak. "When you demanded I open the vault earlier... you were suspecting that Da-ge's head was in my possession?"

Lan Xichen’s head hung lower, swallowed by remorse.

Jin Guangyao looked down, hugging his wife's corpse to his chest. After an agonizing pause, he murmured, "...Never mind. Let it go. But Er-ge, how did Hanguang-jun know this vault existed in my bedchamber? And how could he possibly conclude that Da-ge's head was inside? Koi Tower is heavily guarded; if I had truly done this, would I leave such evidence out in the open for others to find so easily?"

Lan Xichen was entirely at a loss for words.

Beside him, Wei Wuxian couldn't muster a response either. Who could have imagined that in such a tight window, Jin Guangyao hadn't just moved the head—he had somehow manipulated Qin Su into committing public suicide to seal her lips forever!

While his mind raced, Jin Guangyao let out a long, sorrowful sigh. "Xuanyu, was it you who fed these lies to my brother? What was the point of spinning a story that falls apart the moment the doors open?"

A nearby sect leader asked, confused, "Lianfang-zun, who are you talking to?"

Su She chimed in with a sneer, "Who else? The man standing beside Hanguang-jun."

Every eye pivoted toward Wei Wuxian. Su She continued, "Those outside the Lanling Jin Sect may not recognize him. His name is Mo Xuanyu, an outcast disciple of our house. He was expelled years ago for disgraceful conduct and harassing Lianfang-zun. Yet recently, he somehow caught Hanguang-jun's eye, accompanying him everywhere. Why Hanguang-jun, a paragon of virtue, would harbor such a creature is truly beyond comprehension."

Jin Ling’s face twisted in embarrassment and anger. Amidst the hushed whispers, Jin Guangyao laid his wife's body down and rose slowly to his feet, resting his palm on Hensheng's hilt as he took a step forward. "I will not dwell on past grievances, but tell the truth: did you have a hand in A-Su's sudden death?"

The sheer conviction in his voice was staggering—radiating the righteous fury of an innocent man! To the crowd, it sounded as though Mo Xuanyu, harboring a bitter vendetta, had framed the Chief Cultivator and bewitched Madame Jin into taking her own life.

Wei Wuxian was completely backed into a corner. What could he possibly say? That he’d seen the head in a secret compartment? That he’d infiltrated the vault as a paper effigy? Name the mystery informant who had spoken to a dead woman? Mention an anonymous letter that had already been burned to ash? Any defense would only dig his grave deeper!

While his thoughts whirled, Hensheng cleared its scabbard! Lan Wangji stepped into the breach, Bichenintercepting the strike with a violent screech of steel.

Seeing the clash, the surrounding cultivators drew their swords, two blades lunging at Wei Wuxian’s flank. Unarmed, he glanced over his shoulder—and spotted Suibian resting on the shelf. He snatched the hilt and drew the blade!

Jin Guangyao’s eyes widened in horror. He cried out, "The Yiling Laozu!"

In the blink of an eye, every sword in the room whipped around to point straight at his chest.

Including Jin Ling's!

Called out by name, Wei Wuxian stared at Jin Ling's shattered, bewildered expression, the tip of Suihuatrembling before his eyes.

Jin Guangyao pressed his advantage, projecting his voice across the chamber: "To think the Yiling Laozu has returned to the mortal realm. Pardon our failure to offer a proper welcome!"

Wei Wuxian was entirely at a loss—how had he blown his cover?

Nie Huaisang groaned groggily from the floor, "Third Brother... who are you shouting at? Isn't that Mo Xuanyu?"

Jin Guangyao kept his sword leveled at Wei Wuxian. "Huaisang, A-Ling, get behind me! Be on your guard, everyone—he drew that sword! He is undeniably the Yiling Laozu, Wei Wuxian!"

Because the true name of Wei Wuxian's sword was so utterly absurd to say aloud, people had always referred to it ambiguously as "that sword" or "his blade". But the name Yiling Laozu carried a dread far more terrifying than Nie Mingjue’s dismembered ghost. Cultivators who hadn't even intended to draw steel reflexively unsheathed their weapons, forming a wall of blades around the vault.

Nie Huaisang stammered, "Does pulling a sword automatically make someone the Yiling Laozu? Brothers, Hanguang-jun... isn't this just a massive misunderstanding?"

"There is no misunderstanding," Jin Guangyao declared. "He is Wei Wuxian."

Jin Ling cried out, frantic, "Wait! Uncle, wait! Jiujiu, didn't you lash him with Zidian back on Dafan Mountain?! His soul wasn't pulled out—he couldn't have stolen this body! It might not be him!"

Jiang Cheng’s face was dark as thunder, his hand resting white-knuckled on his hilt, silent as his mind churned.

Jin Guangyao countered, "Dafan Mountain? Ah, thank you for the reminder, A-Ling. Who was the one who summoned Wen Ning that night?"

Jin Ling paled, his defense crumbling.

Jin Guangyao turned to the crowd. "What you do not know is that while Xuanyu was still a disciple on Koi Tower, he stumbled upon an old manuscript belonging to the Yiling Laozu in my collection. That manuscript detailed the forbidden ritual of Sacrificial Summoning—trading one's own flesh and soul to summon a vengeful spirit to enact revenge. Sect Leader Jiang could strike him a hundred times with Zidian and it would reveal nothing, because the vessel was offered willingly! It wasn't possession at all!"

The narrative was seamless. Mo Xuanyu, harboring bitter resentment after being expelled, enacted the forbidden ritual to summon the Yiling Laozu for vengeance. Everything Wei Wuxian had done was to avenge his summoner. And if that was the case, Nie Mingjue’s dismemberment was undoubtedly his handiwork as well! Whenever a mystery lacked an answer, pinning it on the Yiling Laozu was always the easiest conclusion.

Yet a few cultivators remained skeptical. "If Sacrificial Summoning leaves no spiritual traces, we cannot condemn him based solely on Lianfang-zun's word."

Jin Guangyao nodded. "The ritual cannot be proven, but his identity can. Ever since the Yiling Laozu was torn apart by his own ghouls atop the Burial Mounds, his personal sword has been kept in the Lanling Jin treasury. Shortly after his death, the sword sealed itself."

Wei Wuxian froze. Sealed itself?

A terrible realization dawned on him.

Jin Guangyao explained, "A sword carries a spiritual soul. It refused to let anyone other than Wei Wuxian wield it, locking its blade tight. For thirteen years, no one has been able to draw it. And just now, this 'Mo Xuanyu' drew that very blade right before your eyes!"

Before the final syllable fell, dozens of swords lunged straight for Wei Wuxian!

Lan Wangji stepped forward, Bichen releasing a concussive shockwave that blasted the attackers backward, clearing an escape path.

Lan Xichen shouted, "Wangji!"

The stumbling sect leaders sputtered in outrage, "Hanguang-jun! You—!"

Wei Wuxian didn't waste a single breath. He vaulted onto the windowsill and dropped lightly into the courtyard, taking off at a dead sprint.

His thoughts raced: The second Jin Guangyao saw that paper effigy and Suibian unsheathed, he deduced my identity on the spot. He fabricated a cover story, manipulated Qin Su into killing herself, and deliberately cornered me by the shelf so I would draw the sword to defend myself! Terrifying... absolutely terrifying how fast he improvises his lies!

Footsteps matched his stride; Lan Wangji had caught up, running silently at his side.

Wei Wuxian’s reputation had been in the gutter for two lifetimes, so he was thoroughly used to mob mentalities. Running was second nature; clear out first, strike back when an opening appeared, and don't sweat it if it didn't. Sticking around to argue was useless; shouting his innocence would only be laughed at. The world was convinced the Yiling Laozu had returned to slaughter the sects, and Jin Guangyao was holding the torch.

Lan Wangji, however, was a completely different story. He didn't even need to make excuses; the world would naturally assume Hanguang-jun had simply been deceived by a cunning villain.

Wei Wuxian panted, "Hanguang-jun, you don't need to follow me!"

Lan Wangji kept his eyes locked ahead, offering no reply as the roar of the lynch mob faded behind them.

Wei Wuxian yelled again, "Are you truly going to run with me?! Think carefully—the second you cross these gates, your pristine reputation is finished!"

They were barreling down the carriage ramp of Koi Tower when Lan Wangji suddenly caught his wrist. He opened his mouth to speak, but a white silhouette flashed before them, cutting off their path.

Jin Ling.

Seeing the boy, Wei Wuxian exhaled in brief relief. But as they tried to sidestep him, Jin Ling pivoted, blocking them again.

"Are you Wei Ying?!"

The boy’s face was a tempest of raw, shattered emotions—eyes rimmed with red, tearing between incandescent fury, bitter hatred, desperate doubt, and agonizing confusion. He screamed again, his voice cracking:

"Are you truly Wei Ying... Wei Wuxian?!"

Looking at the boy, hearing the jagged heartbreak that far outweighed the hatred in his voice, Wei Wuxian’s heart clenched with an ache. But the mob was descending behind them; there was no time to explain. Gritting his teeth, he moved to dodge around him a third time.

Suddenly, a cold shock pierced his gut.

He looked down. Jin Ling was already pulling a blood-stained, snow-white blade from his abdomen.

He truly hadn't expected Jin Ling to actually run him through.

A wry, bitter thought flashed through Wei Wuxian’s mind: Out of everyone in the world, he just had to take after his uncle—even stabbing me in the exact same spot.

The moments that followed were a chaotic blur. He remembered flailing his arms, the roar of the mob, concussive explosions of spiritual energy, and violent tremors rattling through the earth.

When his senses finally stitched themselves back together, his eyes cracked open. Lan Wangji was flying atop Bichen, carrying Wei Wuxian on his back, blood splattered across the pristine porcelain of his cheek.

The wound in his gut didn't throb with unbearable agony, but it was a hole through his flesh nonetheless. He had held on through sheer willpower, but Mo Xuanyu’s fragile vessel had never sustained a mortal wound; the relentless blood loss had dragged him into unconsciousness despite his best efforts.

Wei Wuxian rasped weakly, "...Lan Zhan."

Lan Wangji’s breathing was noticeably heavier than usual—uneven and hurried from flying with a wounded passenger while fending off pursuers. Yet his response was steady as an anchor, identical to the past:

"Mm."

After that single syllable, he added softly, "I am here."

Hearing those three words, a sensation Wei Wuxian had never experienced in either of his lives welled up in his chest—a sharp, tender ache, both burning and warm.

He still remembered their falling out in Jiangling, when Lan Wangji had ridden hundreds of miles to offer aid, only for Wei Wuxian to reject him with bitter barbs and furious pride.

Back then, when the entire world feared and flattered him, Lan Wangji was the only one who dared scold him to his face.

And now, when the entire world spat upon and despised him, Lan Wangji was the only one standing by his side.

A sudden memory surfaced, and Wei Wuxian murmured, "Ah... I remember now."

Lan Wangji asked, "Remember what?"

Wei Wuxian leaned his forehead against his back, whispering softly, "I remember now, Lan Zhan. Just like this... I really did carry you on my back once."
